Honestly given the huge negativity around this game I wasn't really sure what to expect going in. Certainly some bugs and weird crashes and it did not dissapoint there, but some tweaks and turning rtx off resolved those.  Beyond that though it was kind of an open question.

The actual game is no where near as bad as I had feared though, it was actually fairly engaging and rather fun, at least as a single player game.  I generally avoided any multiplayer aspect and just treated it like a giant escort quest except honestly your more often the one being escorted than not.  The computer player will be knocked down from time to time but they probably saved me 10 times for every time I saved them.

The core game loop, running missions through the same maps but with slightly tweaked scenarios was not actually all that bad.  It felt almost a little like deathloop except much much more guns blazing action.  The main complaint I'd have is that really a large number of the weapons are pretty useless outside of specific functions/access they give you.  You will spend the majority of the game playing with the same 2-3 weapons and enemies will generally be pretty spongy and soak in way more bullets than seems reasonable at times.

Its not anything you can't handle, but it takes something away from the impact of a super powerful rotating barrel auto shotgun if it still takes half a dozen headshots with it to take down a good portion of the enemies later in the game, etc.

Beyond that though I actually did enjoy continuing the BJ story through his daughters, I liked the nods to 80s tech thrown around, and overall I think if they had just made this a single player game and spent a little more time cleaning up some of the more nasty bugs, it honestly would be a perfectly fine and fun shooter.

I recommend it for folks who have liked the more modern wolfenstein games, but with the caveat you temper your expectations and focus on it like a single player game, and it'll play ok in the end.

A decent concept that is poorly executed. First off, I played most the game solo since trying to get someone to play the game with you is harder than the entire game. Even in coop its kind of laggy and its a real pain to use the bethesda.net social platform. It is more than playable solo even though the ally ai can be really stupid and even get you caught in stealth. Quick verdict, if you like Wolfenstein then it might be worth a playthrough since it is only 8 hours long with side content and there are some interesting lore drops but not worth it past that.
Gunplay in the game feels great and terrible at the same time. It feels as though someone took the really fun parts of the last game and put them with a really stupid armor system. Armor itself is really what takes the game to passable to downright frustrating. Having to switch guns to even try and damage some enemies really feels terrible. Having Hanz the Handyman able to sit there and take entire mags from a machine pistol just because he has a square health bar instead of a rectangle one kills the pacing of firefights. This can be fixed later in the game where you just have super op guns and level them up but that is also another issue. Leveling guns seems like a good idea but it led to me just using two or three guns maybe until I got the super guns when I just almost exclusively used them instead. It leads to a snowballing effect where one gun starts to feel really good and fun to use but the rest just feel terrible as you reload three times to kill one guy with armor.
That said, I feel the best part of the game is the art direction. They really nailed it with every location I feel, the only issue is that the only location is Paris. Granted there are some side streets, nicer parts of town and some facilities but its still all Paris. That said, they did their best to shake up the designs of some of the locations and the weapons and enemies look pretty good. It is nice that the enemies change as you level up but does not really make any sense. With RTX they really did let the artists shine though making it easily the best part of the game even if they really did not play up the 80s aspect. It really just looks like the 60s with a few more futuristic elements but still a visually pleasing game. With that, performance was also alright but still managed to drop below the 120 fps mark but I did play on the highest settings so that is kind of understandable.
For me, this game is a disappointment. I'm not sure what player audience it was intended for, but having played previous Wolfenstein games, this is too far off from the original story flow.

The trilogy of Wolfenstein: Old Blood/New Order/New Colossus is a brilliant fever dream of Scandanavians imagining what Americans are like at its best and worst and putting that into an excellent and wonderfully bloody game of killing lots and lots and lots of Nazis. It is one of the few games I consider truly works of art. 

Wolfenstein: Youngblood is...just a computer game. It has a few moments, but I can't get up the interest to complete it. It's not the gameplay that is the problem, I could see the exact same gameplay being excellent. It's the writing. It has none of the spirit of the trilogy, only its superficial trappings. This is not a game where you will briefly see the multicolored gecko of hallucination, or a blood soaked pregnant woman blasting away topless at Nazi fiends, or where have your own head chopped off and wonder what the heck is going to happen next.

There is a moment in the first 10 minutes, where the twins are both sickened and excited by their first murder of a Nazi that shows a game that could have been, but wasn't.

Wolfenstein in co-op is a great idea... unfortunately, unnecessary lite-RPG mechanics get in the way (on top of disastrous writing—seriously, the main characters just act like... kids).

The gunplay is still excellent, co-op is genuinely fun with a friend, and blasting Nazis never gets old. Sadly, the leveling system, enemy health bars, and RPG progression hurt the game's pacing and overall gamefeel. Instead of rewarding skill, the game too often relies on bullet sponge enemies and arbitrary level requirements.

It's still enjoyable in co-op, but it lacks the tight, satisfying gameplay that made The New Order / Old Blood and The New Colossus so memorable. A fun spin-off with wasted potential.
